analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md, in the Runtime constants table (head lines 2009-2012). It repoints the reconnect-backoff source to CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift and adds rows for: a backoff reset after a 60 s stable session counted from the register frame, and a random 0-1 s reconnect wait after WebSocket close code 1012. The ping/pong row now cites CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift on its own. No code, config defaults, keys, trust boundaries or mitigations change.

The documented behavior touches TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket) availability only. Keeping a 0-1 s reconnect wait for 1012 (service restart) with no backoff growth is a design choice made in unseen source. The coordinator is trusted, so a hostile 1012 storm would need a compromised or impersonated coordinator, and TLS is not changed here. The stable-session reset counted from the register frame is also unverified. A provider that registers and is then dropped could in principle hold the backoff near its minimum, which is a coordinator load concern. That cannot be confirmed from this doc-only change.

I saw no new secrets, endpoints, attestation, encryption, or authorization claims. The unchanged context (cache, App Attest, fan control) is pre-existing and not modified. Open integration question: whether CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift matches these documented constants and sits outside any threat-model-relevant retry path (T-057 availability). That source was not supplied, so the doc accuracy is unverified. No finding qualifies.
